steps.name: Install Swift toolchain (robust discovery + verification)
steps.description: Install a minimal Swift Linux toolchain into /opt/swift if missing. The script tries a pinned SWIFT_VERSION first and then a short fallback list; for each candidate it discovers an available ubuntu24.04 tarball in the corresponding release directory, downloads the tarball and the upstream checksum file, selects the checksum line for the chosen tarball and verifies with sha256sum -c, extracts atomically to /opt/swift, and persists PATH and CI-friendly variables via /etc/profile.d/swift.sh. Only minimal apt packages are installed. This step is idempotent and fails with clear diagnostics if no usable toolchain could be discovered or verified. Operates in the workspace: /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-app-323487-323496/calculator_frontend
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-app-323487-323496/calculator_frontend"
INSTALL_DIR="/opt/swift"
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
cd "$TMP"
sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates xz-utils libatomic1 >/dev/null
# configurable primary version and small fallback list
SWIFT_PRIMARY="5.9.4"
FALLBACKS=("5.9.4" "5.9.3" "5.9.0" "5.8.5")
BASE_URL="https://download.swift.org/swift"
# if already installed and matches one of our candidates, skip
if [ -x "$INSTALL_DIR/usr/bin/swift" ]; then
  INST_VER=$($INSTALL_DIR/usr/bin/swift --version 2>/dev/null | awk '/Swift version/ {print $3; exit}' || true)
  for v in "${FALLBACKS[@]}"; do [ "$INST_VER" = "$v" ] && { echo "swift $INST_VER already installed"; rm -rf "$TMP"; exit 0; }; done
fi
# try candidates until one succeeds
SUCCESS=0
for SWIFT_VERSION in "${FALLBACKS[@]}"; do
  RELEASE_DIR="$BASE_URL/${SWIFT_VERSION}-release"
  # prefer ubuntu24.04 named tarballs
  LIST_URL="$RELEASE_DIR/"
  # fetch listing (fallback to index redirect)
  HTML=$(curl -fsS --retry 2 "$LIST_URL" || true)
  if [ -z "$HTML" ]; then continue; fi
  TARBALL=$(printf "%s" "$HTML" | grep -oP 'swift-[^\"'> ]+ubuntu24.04.tar.gz' | head -n1 || true)
  if [ -z "$TARBALL" ]; then
    # try less strict match
    TARBALL=$(printf "%s" "$HTML" | grep -oP 'swift-[^\"'> ]+ubuntu24.04[^\"'> ]*\.tar\.gz' | head -n1 || true)
  fi
  [ -n "$TARBALL" ] || continue
  TARBALL_URL="$RELEASE_DIR/$TARBALL"
  # download tarball and checksum file
  curl --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -fsS -O "$TARBALL_URL" || { rm -f "$TARBALL"; continue; }
  # possible checksum filenames: SHA256SUMS, sha256sums.txt, SHA256SUMS.sig
  for SUMNAME in SHA256SUMS sha256sums.txt SHA256SUMS.txt; do
    curl --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -fsS -O "$RELEASE_DIR/$SUMNAME" || true
  done
  # find a matching checksum line in any downloaded file
  MATCH_LINE=$(grep -h "$TARBALL" SHA256SUMS* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  if [ -z "$MATCH_LINE" ]; then
    # cleanup and continue to next candidate
    rm -f "$TARBALL" SHA256SUMS* || true
    continue
  fi
  # prepare checksum file in 'sha256  filename' format
  CHECKFILE="${TMP}/${TARBALL}.sha256"
  echo "$MATCH_LINE" | awk '{print $1 "  " $2}' > "$CHECKFILE"
  sha256sum -c "$CHECKFILE" >/dev/null || { rm -f "$TARBALL" SHA256SUMS* "$CHECKFILE"; continue; }
  # verified, extract atomically
  EXTRACT_DIR="${TMP}/swift-extract"
  mkdir -p "$EXTRACT_DIR"
  tar -xzf "$TARBALL" -C "$EXTRACT_DIR" --strip-components=1
  sudo rm -rf "${INSTALL_DIR}.old" || true
  if [ -d "$INSTALL_DIR" ]; then sudo mv "$INSTALL_DIR" "${INSTALL_DIR}.old"; fi
  sudo mv "$EXTRACT_DIR" "$INSTALL_DIR"
  sudo rm -rf "${INSTALL_DIR}.old" || true
  # persist PATH and CI
  sudo tee /etc/profile.d/swift.sh >/dev/null <<'EOF'
# Swift toolchain
export PATH=/opt/swift/usr/bin:${PATH}
export CI=true
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
EOF
  sudo chmod +x /etc/profile.d/swift.sh
  export PATH=/opt/swift/usr/bin:${PATH}
  SUCCESS=1
  break
done
rm -rf "$TMP"
if [ "$SUCCESS" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: failed to find/verify a compatible swift toolchain. Tried: ${FALLBACKS[*]}" >&2
  exit 10
fi
# validate
command -v swift >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: swift not on PATH after install" >&2; exit 11; }
command -v swiftc >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: swiftc not found" >&2; exit 12; }
swift --version || true

reasoning: Goal: provide a minimal, headless Swift development environment inside the running Ubuntu 24.04 container at the provided workspace. Primary constraint from engineer feedback: the install script's strict pin (swift-5.9.4) and filename discovery caused checksum mismatches when the SHA file didn't contain the expected filename. To resolve this I modified the install step to use a robust discovery strategy: query the release directory for any matching 'ubuntu24.04' tarball, pick the first matching release tarball that also has a checksum entry (or try a small set of fallback Swift versions), verify via the SHA file entry that matches the chosen filename, and only then install. This avoids hard-failing on minor naming differences between release directories and upstream checksum file formats. I preserved idempotency (skip when /opt/swift matches the desired version) and persisted PATH via /etc/profile.d/swift.sh. The scaffolding step is preserved but ensured to check swift presence; it creates a pure-Swift library Calculator and a long-running calc-demo executable for deterministic start/stop validation along with tests. I added an explicit 'install-fallback-001' behaviour inside the install script (try configured SWIFT_VERSION first, then try a small fallback list) to address network/naming issues without requiring architect interaction. The test and validation steps were adjusted to fail-fast with clear diagnostics if swift couldn't be installed. All scripts follow the required shebang, set -euo pipefail and operate using the supplied workspace path. I kept total steps minimal (environment/install, scaffold, test, validation/start combined) to satisfy the planning constraints while addressing the blocking checksum issue.
